newsitem.title: USA: Chicago Fed Index up 0.5 pct to 128.9 in July.
newsitem.headline: Chicago Fed Index up 0.5 pct to 128.9 in July.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago said its newly revised and updated Chicago Fed Midwest Manufacturing Index (CFMMI) rose 0.5 percent in July to a record high reading of 128.9.

"July's performance marked the third solid gain in the CFMMI since its sharp rebound from the General Motors strike in March, and the third time in the last four months that the Chicago Fed Index has outpaced the nation," said a report issued by the Chicago Fed.
The July gain was nearly twice that of the national rate as measured by the manufacturing component of the Federal Reserve Board's U.S. Industrial Production Index (IPMFG), the report said.
The Chicago Fed said that the driving force behind the region's strong showing in July was the auto sector, which posted a 3.0 percent gain.

The report said it represented the auto sector's largest increase since its 12.4 percent rebound in April, following the March auto strike. Other sectors in the Midwest were relatively flat and more closely mirrored their national counterparts, according to the report.

"The (auto) industry is pretty much at capacity, and that's going to suggest that as we get into August, where the seasonals are going to make it tougher for the industry, that we'll see this moderating from its July pace," said Robert Schnorbus, senior Chicago Fed economist, at a Chicago Fed briefing on revisions to the index.
